cluster_summary: This cluster contains 18 Netty CVEs covering a range of input parsing and validation flaws, including missing CRLF validation, disabled header validation, insufficient boundary checks, resource exhaustion, memory leaks, and incorrect protocol state handling. The vulnerabilities span HTTP, SMTP, WebSocket, AJP, and binary HTTP parsers.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the guard is enforced before the sensitive effect and remains bound to the same resource, principal, destination, or object that the effect uses. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Add a call to validateValue after converting each element in the bulk setObject methods..

mechanism.name: Bypass of header validation in bulk set

mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Add a call to validateValue after converting each element in the bulk setObject methods.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Add a call to validateValue after converting each element in the bulk setObject methods.
sub_patterns.name: Bypass of header validation in bulk set
sub_patterns.root_cause: The setObject methods for iterable and varargs inputs loop over elements and add them without invoking validateValue, bypassing the per-value validation that the single-value setter applies.
